references.text: The goat as a sin offering is prescribed in Leviticus for the sins of leaders, showing the same sacrificial practice of using goats as sin offerings.
A goat as a sin offering is also mentioned here in connection with the consecration of the tabernacle.
On the Day of Atonement, a goat was also to be used as a sin offering, demonstrating the use of goats in the context of sin offerings.
A goat as a sin offering for the entire congregation is mentioned here, along with burnt offerings and drink offerings.
The daily burnt offering (tamid) mentioned in verse 15 is described in detail here, including the drink offering.
The same wording about a goat as a sin offering for atonement is used during the Feast of Tabernacles.
Goats as sin offerings are mentioned in connection with the temple dedication under Hezekiah.
The letter to the Hebrews explains that the blood of goats and bulls cannot take away sins, but points forward to Christ's perfect sacrifice.
